WEFT-723.name: ws02: BVH × HNSW Phase F join — dual-index composition after ADR-088 VectorRef
WEFT-723.description:
Source
design: docs/design/bvh_schema_updates.md
ADR-056 amendment (2026-07-31) / ADR-088
prior: WEFT-721, WEFT-722 (payload handle insurance)
Problem / gap
ADR-088 reserved an optional VectorRef handle on every spatial leaf payload so WEFT-709 does not ossify pure-geometry leaves. The join itself is still deferred: dual-index query plans (BVH containment ∩ HNSW feature similarity), embedder choice (visual vs language index_ids), and Temporal Similarity Search via HNSW Fingerprinting from the ADR-056 concept paper §10.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] ADR for BVH × HNSW composition (or explicit reject with rationale)
[ ] Consumer path that resolves VectorRef after a spatial query (or filters HNSW hits by leaf id)
[ ] Tests demonstrating join (even fixture-backed) without inlining embeddings into leaves

blocked-by: none for design drafting; implementation after producers populate vector
blocks: none currently
Notes
Do not put embeddings inline in leaves (ADR-088 rejected Option 3). Geometric query_knn already exists; feature k-NN stays on HNSW.

WEFT-722.name: ws02/ws17: BVH leaf embedding decision — should a spatial leaf reference a feature vector, before WEFT-709 mints Objects
WEFT-722.description:
Source
design note (authoritative for this ticket — read this first, do not re-derive from ADRs/code): docs/design/bvh_schema_updates.md
supersedes: WEFT-721, which incorrectly claimed the weftos-leaf-types tag registry and typed payload schemas don't exist yet. They do — WEFT-717 (BVH Phase B) shipped them (crates/weftos-leaf-types/src/spatial/{tags.rs,primitives.rs}, commit 82482e14). See docs/design/bvh_schema_updates.md §2.2 for the correction and citations.
code (for the specific gap this ticket is about): crates/weftos-leaf-types/src/spatial/primitives.rs — ten typed payload structs (SpherePayload, AabbPayload, ObbPayload, CapsulePayload, SweptAabbPayload, FrustumPayload, RadialSphereEventPayload, BeamTracePayload, SensorRead4DPayload, SplatScenePayload); none has an embedding/vector-id/feature field
code: crates/clawft-bvh/src/query.rs — no query_knn at the time the design note was written (verify current state before implementing anything against this ticket; the crate has been under active concurrent development)
Problem / gap
Typed BVH leaf payload schemas exist and are Done (WEFT-717). What's undecided is narrower: whether a spatial leaf references a feature vector at all, and if so how. Today none of the ten payload structs in primitives.rs carry one. The only embedding subsystem in the workspace (E5/Qwen3 → HNSW) is text-only and structurally separate from anything spatial — ADR-056 explicitly defers that join rather than deciding against it.
WEFT-709 (ws17: ADR-078 W1 — geometric partition into surfaces/object AABBs, currently Todo) is the point where real WM_OBJECT/WM_SURFACE leaves start getting minted in volume from every splat capture. Before it, a payload-struct change is a recompile. After it, it's a data migration. That's the entire reason for filing this now rather than waiting.
Explicitly out of scope: choosing an embedding model, building the BVH↔HNSW join or a query_knn-based similarity path, implementing WEFT-709 itself.
Decision to make
Sh

WEFT-721.name: ws02/ws17: BVH leaf payload schema — typed payload + embedding-field decision before WEFT-709 mints Objects
WEFT-721.description:
Source
code: crates/clawft-bvh/src/leaf.rs:19-30 (Leaf.payload is opaque Vec<u8>; tag is pub mod tags marked "registry later, free u32 for now" at leaf.rs:49-73)
code: crates/weftos-leaf-types/src/lib.rs (415 lines; zero spatial content — no spatial module, no tag registry, no embedding field, confirmed by direct read + grep this session)
code: crates/clawft-kernel/src/embedding.rs, embedding_e5.rs, embedding_qwen3.rs, vector_hnsw.rs, hnsw_service.rs (the only embedding+HNSW path in the workspace today — text-only, feeds ECC causal-graph/agent-context search, structurally disconnected from anything spatial)
ADR: docs/adr/adr-056-bvh-spatial-index.md §3 (tagged-union leaf registry), §8 (SpatialBackend trait — no query_knn-adjacent embedding hook), and the Neutral consequence explicitly deferring "BVH + HNSW composition (Temporal Similarity Search via HNSW Fingerprinting, concept paper §10)" to a future ADR
doc: docs/weftos/splat-to-world-model.md §3.3 (sketch WM_OBJECT payload JSON — design-only, not implemented; no embedding field in the sketch either)
research: .planning/research/cosmos3-vs-weftos-worldmodel.md (three-lane Cosmos-3-vs-WeftOS analysis; relevant conclusions cited, not restated — see Notes)
Problem / gap
Leaf.payload is an untyped byte blob and the tag registry meant to formalize it (weftos-leaf-types) doesn't exist yet for spatial tags. Nothing in the schema currently has an opinion on whether a BVH entity (Object or Event leaf — WM_OBJECT, WM_SURFACE, WM_VOLUME, etc.) carries any embedding reference. Meanwhile WeftOS already runs a real, working text-embedding + HNSW stack (E5/Qwen3 → ONNX → HNSW) that is completely disconnected from the spatial/entity path — ADR-056 explicitly defers the BVH↔HNSW composition question rather than deciding it.
WEFT-709 (ws17: ADR-078 W1 — geometric partition into surfaces/object AABBs, currently Todo) is the point where real WM_OBJECT/WM_SURFACE leaves start getting minted at volume. Once that lands, the payload shap

WEFT-684.name: ws06: memory — MCP server runs 'npx ruflo@latest', so a schema-bearing dep is unpinned (root cause of WEFT-669)
WEFT-684.description:
Source
~/.claude.json → mcpServers.ruflo.command = "npx",
  args = ["-y", "ruflo@latest", "mcp", "start"]
installed alternatives: ~/Library/pnpm/bin/ruflo = 3.14.1;
  ~/.nvm/.../bin/ruflo → symlink to the dev checkout ~/dev/ruflo/ruflo/bin/ruflo.js
  = 3.32.38 (branch feat/grok-host, dirty tree); npm latest = 3.32.39
the project's own recorded rule: use the GLOBAL binary, never
  npx ruflo@latest, "which runs its own private copy and hides drift"
consequence already paid: WEFT-669 (the AgentDB store split)
Problem / gap
The claude-flow/ruflo MCP server — which owns .swarm/agentdb-memory.db, the
project's memory store — is configured to launch via npx -y ruflo@latest.
That means the version serving the memory store is **whatever npm publishes at
the moment of invocation**, re-resolved every session, chosen by nobody. Three
other ruflo installs exist on this machine at three different versions, and none
of them is the one actually running.
This is the pattern the project's own operating notes explicitly forbid, and it
is the most probable root cause of WEFT-669: AgentDB was recreated under a new
filename (agentdb-memory.db) when a newer ruflo introduced the
provenance_type column (ADR-323), stranding all 188 entries in the old
memory.db — clawft-knowledge, ruv/brain, and every weftos/* namespace
became unretrievable. Nobody decided to take that migration. npx took it.
So "update agentdb" is the wrong frame: it already updates itself, continuously
and invisibly. The defect is that a schema-bearing dependency is unpinned.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Pin the MCP server to an explicit version — ruflo@3.32.39 rather than
      ruflo@latest — so schema changes become a decision with a changelog read,
      not a surprise discovered later by a missing namespace
[ ] Decide which install is canonical and remove or rename the others. Three
      binaries at 3.14.1 / 3.32.38 / npx-latest means "which ruflo ran?" is
      unanswerable after the fact, and PATH order silently decides
[

WEFT-683.name: ws02: mesh — ADR-031 drift: RVF encoding declared the production default but only JSON was ever built
WEFT-683.description:
Source
ADR: docs/adr/ — ADR-031 (Status: Accepted), dual JSON/RVF encoding for
  KernelMessage, RVF stated as the production default for performance
code: mesh_ipc.rs:47 — unconditional serde_json::to_vec
closed ticket that covered the JSON half: WEFT-110 (Done, correctly)
Problem / gap
ADR-031 is Accepted and decided a dual-encoding scheme: JSON for
debuggability, RVF (type byte 0x02) as the production default for
performance. Only the JSON half was built.
mesh_ipc.rs:47 unconditionally calls serde_json::to_vec. There is no RVF
encoding path and no type-byte switch anywhere in the mesh wire code.
WEFT-110 is correctly Done — its three literal acceptance criteria (ADR exists,
JSON encoding is ADR-sanctioned, round-trip test exists) are all met, and it is
not being reopened. But its title reads "JSON vs RVF", so the tracker currently
implies both paths exist.
Per this repo's standing rule that ADRs are living plans, not stale paper,
an Accepted ADR describing an unbuilt production default is exactly the drift
that rule exists to catch: the plan and the code disagree, and the plan is the
one asserting something untrue.
Acceptance criteria
Pick one of these two and complete it — the point is that ADR-031 and the
code stop disagreeing:
Option A — amend the ADR (cheap, honest):
[ ] Update ADR-031 with an Updated: date and a note that the RVF path was
      deferred, with the reason
[ ] State what would trigger building it (a measured JSON encoding cost, a
      throughput target), so the deferral is revisitable rather than permanent
Option B — build the RVF path:
[ ] Type-byte dispatch in the mesh wire format (0x01 JSON / 0x02 RVF)
[ ] RVF encode/decode for KernelMessage, round-trip tested
[ ] Production default flips to RVF as the ADR specifies, with JSON retained
      for debugging
[ ] A benchmark showing the performance claim that motivated the decision
Dependencies
related: WEFT-110 (Done — the JSON half; left closed deliberately)
Notes
Recommend Option A unless mes

WEFT-682.description:
Source
2026-07-29 Plane↔git reconciliation sweep, label-coverage analysis
affected set: 36 items, concentrated from WEFT-556 onward
Problem / gap
The project rule requires every work item to carry two labels: a workstream
(wsNN-*) and a finding-type (bug/gap/stub/orphan/governance/
tech-debt/docs/tests/tooling). 36 items violate it: 20 missing both, 14
missing the workstream, 2 missing the type.

sweep — are fully labeled. Essentially every item from WEFT-556 onward (the
post-audit development wave from ~2026-06-28) is under-labeled.
So labeling discipline did not decay gradually; it stopped when items stopped
being created by the batch triage process. Ad-hoc item creation during
development does not carry the labeling step, because the discipline lived in the
triage protocol rather than in the creation path.
Cost: labels are the only cross-cutting filter. Without a workstream label an
item is invisible to "what's outstanding in voice?", which is how the 0.7.0 audit
findings were made navigable in the first place.
Acceptance criteria

      apply and verify, don't re-derive)
[ ] Make the creation path enforce it, rather than relying on memory —
      the realistic options: make --labels required in
      scripts/plane.sh create-issue, or extend scripts/plane.sh check to fail
      on label gaps and run it in the pre-commit/handoff flow
[ ] scripts/plane.sh check returns clean for label coverage

      triage step, which is why ad-hoc creation skips it)

  passing, either the advisory cleared or the gate is not failing on it — both

The AgentDB/ruvector memory store existed as two files with the same schema,
and the CLI and the MCP server disagreed about which was authoritative:
| File | Entries | Last written | Schema |
|---|---|---|---|

| .swarm/agentdb-memory.db | live | current | has provenance_type (ADR-323) |

WEFT-667.name: ws13: edge-pad firmware — tilde-pin esp-hal/esp-radio (unstable feature + caret pin is a latent break)
WEFT-667.description:
Source
code: crates/clawft-edge-pad/Cargo.toml:23-27 (esp-hal), :53-60 (esp-radio)
upstream policy: https://github.com/esp-rs/esp-hal — README stability section
brain note: .planning/embedded-rust/brain/notes/11-pitfalls-and-faq.md §2
brain note: .planning/embedded-rust/brain/notes/12-weftos-anchors.md §3
memory chunk: er-unstable-caret-pinning-trap (namespace embedded-rust)
Problem / gap
clawft-edge-pad enables the unstable cargo feature on both esp-hal and
esp-radio, but pins them with caret requirements (version = "1.0.0",
version = "0.17.0"). esp-hal's published stability policy is that **breaking
changes to unstable APIs ship in MINOR releases**, and upstream therefore
recommends the tilde operator for any crate depending on unstable:
esp-hal = { version = "~1.1" }
esp-hal 1.1.0 is already released, so ^1.0.0 currently permits a minor
bump that is explicitly allowed to break the unstable API this firmware relies
on (it uses psram, DMA/LCD_CAM-adjacent paths, and much else that is
unstable-gated — only init + GPIO/UART/SPI/I2C + time are stable in 1.0).
Cargo.lock is what protects the build today; the tilde pin is what
protects it from a careless cargo update. This is latent, not currently
breaking — which is exactly why it should be fixed while it is cheap.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] crates/clawft-edge-pad/Cargo.toml pins esp-hal = { version = "~1.0", ... }
[ ] Same file pins esp-radio = { version = "~0.17", ... }
[ ] Any other in-repo crate enabling an esp-* unstable feature is audited
      and given the same treatment (check crates/lgfx-bus-rgb-rs/Cargo.toml)
[ ] Firmware still builds after the change (Cargo.lock unchanged in
      practice — this is a constraint tightening, not a version move)
[ ] A short comment in the manifest states WHY tilde (so a future tidy-up
      does not revert it)

WEFT-661.name: vector: HybridBackend merges cosine (hot) and sqeuclidean (cold) raw distances — recall 0.113 with real DiskANN
WEFT-661.description: Found by the WEFT-366 bench harness (2026-07-14): with --features diskann, HybridBackend's hot tier (HNSW) scores cosine while the cold tier (real DiskANN) scores squared-Euclidean, and vector_hybrid.rs merge_results sorts raw distances with no scale normalization — cosine hits structurally dominate regardless of true proximity. Measured recall@10 = 0.113 at 10K/384d (vs 0.943 HNSW-only, 0.994 DiskANN-only). Under default features the cold stub is also cosine, masking the bug. Fix candidates: normalize scores to a common scale, unify the metric across tiers, or rank-fuse (RRF) instead of distance-sort. Related: WEFT-126, WEFT-366.

WEFT-659.name: voice: unclear-input gate — consume STT confidence/SNR/paralinguistics before engaging the brain
WEFT-659.description: Hot-mic feedback (2026-07-14): garbage STT ('If that shoes is a some sort of weird gap...') became a full agent turn despite token-conf mean 0.44/min 0.34, SNR 6.4dB, prosody-dsp low — and 'Mm.' (paralinguistics non-lexical/filler) got a full brain reply while idle. Gate BOTH sides from the Wave-1 decomposition: non-lexical classes (backchannel_candidate/laughter_candidate/filler) never dispatch the brain (idle=ignore, busy=existing backchannel arc); low-clarity utterances (long + low token-conf, or very low conf, or low SNR + low conf) get a rotating spoken 'didn't catch that' client-side instead of a brain call, and the daemon voice loop skips dispatch symmetrically. Thresholds are first-cut constants — tune from live traces.

WEFT-653.name: ws11: hermes loop — retained-output review gate: M2 design amendment (Speculative→review→Committed|Discarded)

prior planning: .planning/hermes-loop/m2-daemon-ecc-loop-design.md §2.5
Problem / gap
The ECC forest lifecycle commits turns Frontier→Committed with no review gate between. Amend the M2 design with the gated lifecycle Frontier → Speculative → (review) → Committed | Discarded, a policy enum (auto = today's commit-on-tick; review = hold at Speculative until accept/discard; discard-on-timeout guard), and codify the invariant: a changeset is a view over the trace, never a second store (consistent with M3 one-store goal).

Tool-arg schema hint in the error result (echo the expected canvas command schema back to the model, not just "missing field").
Repeated-identical-failure circuit breaker in run_tool_loop: N identical (tool, error) pairs → abort the loop with a synthetic "stop calling this tool" system nudge or fail fast.

WEFT-640.name: Real embedder: e5-small-v2 + record verbalization (replace SimHash placeholder)

Problem: the kernel HNSW anchor path embeds with a deterministic SimHash placeholder (weave.toml:29, [kernel.agent] comment: "neighbours are not semantic; a future change will route through a real embedder"). Semantic recall quality over node records (classification v2 blobs, VoiceAnalysis, spawn records) is gated on this.
Proposal:
1. Verbalization layer (TabSTAR's idea, adopted not licensed): render structured node records to stable semantic strings (act: question | topic: voice-tts | arousal: high (0.8) | ..., quantile-binned numerics for scalar-heavy VoiceAnalysis fields) and embed the string.
2. Backbone: intfloat/e5-small-v2 — 384-d (matches RVF/HNSW dim exactly), MIT, existing ONNX exports, fits the ~/.weftos/models pattern; wire behind the existing EmbeddingProvider trait.
3. Benchmark vs the SimHash placeholder on recall over real committed node records (graft quality: "find turns like this one — similar act+arousal+topic").
Acceptance: e5-small-v2 ONNX staged + EmbeddingProvider impl + verbalizer for classification/voice_analysis records; recall benchmark documented; flag-gated swap of the anchor/session-tier embedding path.

WEFT-639.name: plane.sh wrapper fixes: WEFT-N resolution, real assignee lookup, cycle-membership via issue.cycle_id
WEFT-639.description:
Source

discovered during the 2026-07-05 full-board Plane sync (WEFT-615..638 + WEFT-606 close)
Problem / gap
Three operational defects in the plane.sh wrapper, each hit and worked around during the 2026-07-05 sync (scripts/plane.py was NOT modified in that run):
transition / close / comment take an issue UUID, not the WEFT-N sequence id. These subcommands PATCH/POST /issues/{arg}/ directly, so passing WEFT-603 hits /issues/WEFT-603/ and 404s. The SKILL/runbook examples ($P close WEFT-603 ...) are therefore wrong as written — you must resolve WEFT-N → UUID first.
--assignee me resolves to the wrong identity. _resolve_user returns members[0].member or members[0].id; every workspace member has member=null, and members[0] is the GitHub bot (not aepod23). So --assignee me silently assigns the bot. Workaround was aepod23's explicit UUID 0d63f76f-0231-49e8-b81a-b2471bb7b91a.
/cycles/{id}/cycle-issues/ GET pagination is flaky. Full-list membership counts came back as 1 on two separate reads while the raw first page reported count=100 / total_pages=2+. Membership must be verified via each issue's authoritative issue.cycle_id field, not that listing.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] transition / close / comment accept a WEFT-N sequence id and resolve it to the issue UUID internally (UUID still accepted)
[ ] --assignee me resolves the authenticated key owner via a real get-me lookup (or config), never members[0]

WEFT-610.name: Talk-Mode said only 'One sec' — silent slow TTS + self-barge-in + premature capture resume
WEFT-610.description: Live: every question got the fast ack then silence; ghost acks every minute. Causes: (1) Ollama orpheus-tts yields zero decodable SNAC frames and DualLayerTts had no fallback; (2) bot barged in on its own ack echo (conversational gate) cancelling every answer; (3) sub-250ms noise blips reached STT earning spurious acks; (4) play_chunk queues only — capture resumed mid-playback and transcribed the bot's own answer as user turns. Fixed in 0c563977: fast-tier answer fallback, floor+15dB barge gate + 400ms grace, min-turn guard, TtsSink::wait_drained wall-clock playback deadline + frame discard. Verified live: 1 turn → 1 audible answer, zero echo turns in 50s. Follow-up: Orpheus/Ollama produces no audio tokens (needs its own investigation); brain confirmed hermes-4.3-36b :8090 per ADR-060.

WEFT-609.name: Talk-Mode deaf in a loud room — fixed -45 dBFS VAD gate vs -37 dBFS room tone

WEFT-605.name: exec_shell security allowlist is invisible to the model — denial spiral burns max tool iterations
WEFT-605.description:
Problem
The exec_shell security allowlist is invisible to the model. Verifying the hermes loop, the question "what is 17 * 23?" drove Hermes into a 20-iteration tool-call spiral — bc, perl, ruby, php, dc, expr, calc, let, whoami — every command rejected by clawft_tools::shell_tool security policy with command not allowed, until max tool iterations (20) exceeded failed the turn. The model gets a bare denial with no hint of what IS allowed, so it keeps guessing.
Observed 2026-07-02 on feat/hermes-loop-base against Hermes 4.3-36B (log in docs/handoff-local-llm-config.md resolution section).
Candidate fixes (pick during implementation)
Include the allowlist (or a policy summary) in the exec_shell tool description so the model knows the boundary up front.
Return the allowlist in the denial error text ("command not allowed; allowed: …").
Count repeated policy denials and short-circuit the turn with a clear message well before max-iterations.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] A denied exec_shell call gives the model enough signal to stop retrying blind variants
[ ] The 17*23 prompt against a tool-happy local model completes without burning max-iterations

WEFT-604.name: Unify local-LLM endpoint/model config — one source of truth for daemon + weft agent + voice
WEFT-604.description:
Problem
There is no single source of truth for "which local LLM endpoint + model to use" — three consumers use three different selection mechanisms (full map in docs/handoff-local-llm-config.md):
1. Daemon → [kernel.llm] (service_url/model) → clawft-service-llm::LlmClient (env LLM_SERVICE_URL, default :8111)
2. weft agent (standalone) → agents.defaults.model (default deepseek/deepseek-chat, cloud) → clawft-llm provider registry; bare model → openai builtin needing a key; LLM_SERVICE_URL ignored on this path
3. LocalProvider::hermes_serving() → hardcoded :8090 (ADR-060) — tests + voice bridge only
Getting the hermes loop running required three machine-local config edits ([kernel.llm], workspace overlay model/routing, [providers.openai] api_base+api_key). A freshly served Hermes (ADR-060, :8090) should be discovered by all three with zero config.
Proper fixes (from the handoff)
Align DEFAULT_LLM_SERVICE_URL (clawft-service-llm/src/lib.rs), the weave.toml/init template, and hermes_serving()/ADR-060 on the same port + default model alias.
Bridge [kernel.llm] → the CLI agent path (as bootstrap.rs:638 does for the daemon), OR route weft agent through the running daemon per ADR-021.
Change the deepseek/deepseek-chat default (clawft-types/src/config/mod.rs:265) to route local when a local endpoint is configured.
Watch out: workspace .clawft/config.json overlay silently overrides weave.toml (most-specific wins) — a stale overlay cost two debugging sessions. Consider logging the winning layer for agents.defaults.model the way the daemon logs the LLM endpoint source.
apply_config_overrides (llm_adapter.rs) has no local/ollama arm — [providers.local] overrides are silently ignored.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Serve Hermes per ADR-060 → daemon, weft agent, and voice loop all reach it with zero machine-local config edits
[ ] Config layer that wins agents.defaults.model is visible in logs
[ ] [providers.local] / [providers.ollama] overrides either work or are rejected loudly

WEFT-603.name: weft agent -m hangs forever after a failed turn (provider error / max-iterations)
WEFT-603.description:
Problem
weft agent -m "…" (single-message mode) hangs forever when the turn fails — provider not configured, max tool iterations exceeded, any pipeline error. The user must ^C. Repro: run without a provider key → ERROR clawft_core::agent::loop_core: failed to process message: provider error: provider not configured → process never exits.
Root cause: AgentLoop::run (crates/clawft-core/src/agent/loop_core.rs:570) logged turn errors and dispatched nothing outbound, while run_single_message (crates/clawft-cli/src/commands/agent.rs) blocks on bus.consume_outbound() for a reply that never comes. Channel users (telegram etc.) likewise got silence on failed turns.
Discovered while verifying the Hermes agent loop (branch feat/hermes-loop-base); documented in docs/handoff-local-llm-config.md (sub-problem C).
Fix
loop_core.rs: the Err arm of the turn match now dispatches an outbound error reply (content = "error: {e}", metadata.error = true) to the originating channel/chat.
agent.rs::run_single_message: recognizes metadata.error, prints to stderr, and exits non-zero (anyhow::bail!). None response also exits non-zero.
Bundled consistency fix: llm_adapter.rs::create_adapter_from_config now honors config.providers.<name>.api_key via resolve_app_api_key (matching create_adapter_for_provider), so a keyless local llama.cpp endpoint behind a builtin's api_base override works with a placeholder key in config instead of requiring the provider's env var.
Acceptance criteria
[x] Provider error → error on stderr, exit 1, <1s (was: infinite hang)
[x] Happy path unchanged: weft agent -m prints answer, exit 0 (verified live against Hermes 4.3-36B on :8090 — Paris, 391)
[x] Workspace suite green: 6760+2 passed / 16 skipped (mdns test env-broken on this network — pre-existing; the 2 clawft-rpc no-daemon tests pass with the daemon stopped)
[x] Doctests green

WEFT-576.name: ws09: deploy — Dockerfile must run as non-root user (security hardening)
WEFT-576.description:
Source
audit-C follow-up audit (.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/follow-up-audit/ws09-dashboard.md), WEFT-317 security pass.
Problem / gap

> "nginx:alpine still needs root to bind 80 and to write the access/error logs, so we keep the default user but disable the daemonize fork (the image's CMD already does this)."
Standard hardening — USER nginx plus listen 8080; plus chown of /var/log/nginx /var/cache/nginx /var/run — was not applied. The audit's security pass explicitly required "runs non-root".
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Dockerfile switches the runtime stage to USER nginx (or a new dedicated user with UID > 1000).
[ ] nginx.conf listens on a high port (e.g. 8080) so root is not needed to bind.
[ ] EXPOSE 8080 (or whatever port is chosen); deployment docs updated to note the port change.
[ ] chown -R nginx:nginx /var/cache/nginx /var/log/nginx /var/run in the build stage so the non-root user can write state.
[ ] scripts/build.sh ui-docker smoke runs the container as the non-root user without errors.
[ ] Image still passes the existing healthcheck.
Dependencies
None.
Notes
Most operators run the image behind a reverse proxy that already does the privileged-port binding, so the high-port move is essentially free in practice.

WEFT-570.name: ws09: auth — logout() must invoke server-side token revoke
WEFT-570.description:
Source
audit-C follow-up audit (.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/follow-up-audit/ws09-dashboard.md), WEFT-309 security pass.
Problem / gap
use-auth.ts::clearStoredToken() only clears localStorage and sets the in-tab clawft-logged-out latch. The Bearer token remains valid against crates/clawft-services/src/api/auth.rs::TokenStore until natural 24h TTL expiry. A token that leaked into a log file (or was screenshot-shared, or copy-pasted) before the user logs out remains usable for the rest of the day. The server-side TokenStore::revoke_token already exists; this is purely a wiring gap.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Server exposes a public route POST /api/auth/revoke that takes the current Bearer token and calls TokenStore::revoke_token.
[ ] Endpoint is on the auth allowlist for itself (no infinite "must be authed to revoke" loop) but requires the Bearer header to identify the token to revoke.
[ ] useAuth().logout() (and clearStoredToken()) POSTs to that endpoint before wiping localStorage. Failure to reach the server is logged but does not block the local clear.
[ ] Test: revoked-then-reused token returns HTTP 401.
[ ] Doc update in docs/ui/api-reference.md.
Dependencies
None — TokenStore::revoke_token and the cleanup task already exist.
Notes
Pair this with WEFT-NEW-E (URL-fragment) so the combined hardening covers both leak prevention and revocation.

WEFT-569.name: ws09: auth — switch ?token= to #token= URL fragment to prevent log leak
WEFT-569.description:
Source
audit-C follow-up audit (.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/follow-up-audit/ws09-dashboard.md), WEFT-309 security pass.
Problem / gap
WEFT-309 enforces single-use inside the browser via consumeUrlToken() + history.replaceState. But the very first GET that fetches index.html carries ?token=<uuid> in the request line, and whatever serves index.html (nginx in the Docker image, Vite in dev, or any reverse proxy) writes that into its access log. Anyone with log read access has a reusable Bearer for the rest of the 24h TTL. The Referer header on subsequent third-party asset fetches before the URL is rewritten is also a leak vector.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] weft ui opens the browser at /#token=<uuid> (URL fragment) instead of /?token=<uuid> (URL query). Browsers do not send fragments to the server, so the token never reaches access logs.
[ ] consumeUrlToken() reads from window.location.hash first, falls back to ?token= for backward compatibility, then strips both via history.replaceState.
[ ] The fragment-mode is documented in docs/ui/api-reference.md as the recommended bootstrap path.
[ ] Bonus: emit a console.warn when a token is observed in the query string instead of the fragment, so we catch any callers that have not migrated.
Dependencies
None.
Notes
This is a one-line change in weft ui plus the consumeUrlToken() parser. Backward compatibility is essentially free.

WEFT-567.name: ws09: ui — /tools route does not call BackendAdapter.getToolSchema for WASM mode
WEFT-567.description:

WEFT-566.description:

Problem / gap

Today bridge.rs::save_config writes to disk and returns Ok; nothing in docs/ui/api-reference.md (or docs/ui/deployment.md) tells the operator whether weft daemon picks up the new config without a restart, or which subset (provider keys? channel toggles?) is hot-reloadable.

[ ] If hot-reload is desired but not yet implemented, file a follow-up and link it from the doc with a clear "Restart required" warning.

WEFT-565.name: ws09: api — TopicBroadcaster topics map leaks empty topic Senders
WEFT-565.description:
Source
audit-C follow-up audit (.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/follow-up-audit/ws09-dashboard.md), WEFT-300 review.
Problem / gap
crates/clawft-services/src/api/broadcaster.rs::TopicBroadcaster.topics is a HashMap that never evicts entries. When a ?topic= is subscribed, the broadcast::Sender stays in the map for the gateway's lifetime even when all subscribers drop. broadcast::Sender prunes dead receivers, but the topic slot itself leaks. Long-running gateways with high-cardinality topic names (e.g. sessions:<uuid>, agents:<id>) accumulate idle channel slots indefinitely.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] When the receiver count for a topic falls to zero AND no producer publishes to it for some grace window, the topic Sender is removed from the topics HashMap.
[ ] OR: publish opportunistically drops topics whose receiver_count() == 0 after the failed send.
[ ] Test that simulates a thousand topic subscriptions+disconnects and asserts the map size returns to baseline.
[ ] Document chosen GC strategy in the broadcaster.rs module comment.
Dependencies
None.
Notes
A grace window matters because a producer may publish before any subscriber arrives — but for sessions:* topics the publisher and subscriber lifecycles are coupled via the session itself, so eviction-on-zero-receivers is safe.

WEFT-564.name: ws16: scripts — actually retire or annotate scripts/check-features.sh (still on disk)

.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/follow-up-audit/ws14-17-deploy-mcp-wasm-research.md (audit-E, 2026-05-01).

-rwxr-xr-x 1 aepod aepod 2352 Apr 22 18:52 scripts/check-features.sh

[ ] Option B: prepend a single deprecation banner to the script:

  # This standalone script will be removed in 0.8.0. The 5 gates here

WEFT-557.name: ws10: SC-4 voice permission flags — gate voice-triggered tool execution by Level 0/1/2
WEFT-557.description:
WEFT-208 — ws10 / SC-4: voice permission flags
Replaces the permission_stub_allows placeholder in
crates/clawft-weave/src/voice_router.rs (shipped by M5-W) with a real
3-level permission grid that gates voice-triggered tool execution.
Permission grid
Level 0 (read-only / unauthenticated voice): chat dispatch
  allowed; command dispatch refused outright.
Level 1 (user / authenticated voice): chat + commands listed in
  voice.consumer.permissions.safe_commands only (defaults
  ["status", "list", "help"]).
Level 2 (privileged): chat + any command, falls through to the
  existing kernel governance gate (gate.check).
Source of voice principal
The substrate publish line carries an actor_id set by
clawft-service-whisper to the source sensor node id. The router reads
it directly from the publish envelope and threads it through
VoiceTurnMetadata.principal. Missing principal → Level 0.
Config (new under `voice.consumer.permissions`)
default_level: u8 (0/1/2; default 0; clamped to 0 if out of range)
principal_levels: HashMap<String, u8> (per-actor_id overrides)
safe_commands: Vec<String> (Level 1 allowlist)
Audit
Every refusal emits a tracing event tagged
event = "voice.permission.denied" carrying principal,
requested_command, level, and reason.
Acceptance criteria
Level 0 transcript → command rejected, chat allowed. ✓
Level 1 transcript with safe command → allowed. ✓
Level 1 transcript with non-safe command → rejected. ✓
Level 2 transcript → reaches the governance-gate downstream
  (CommandHandler trait). ✓
Permission-denied audit event emits with principal + verb + level. ✓
Build
scripts/build.sh check — clean
scripts/build.sh clippy — clean
cargo test -p clawft-weave --lib voice_router — 14 passed
Files
crates/clawft-weave/src/voice_router.rs
crates/clawft-types/src/config/voice.rs
crates/clawft-weave/src/daemon.rs (config → router translation)

WEFT-555.name: ws10: voice — wire substrate STT output into agent conversation + command input
WEFT-555.description:
Source
audit: .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/10-voice.md (referenced in WEFT-205 close)
ADR: docs/adr/adr-053-voice-stt-canonical-path.md (spawned this item)
discussion 2026-04-29: substrate STT pipeline works (sensor → PCM → whisper service → transcript), but nothing in weft consumes the transcript topic
Problem / gap
The substrate STT path is operational on a per-pipeline basis:
clawft-sensor-pipeline runs on a sensor node, captures PCM, publishes on the substrate.
clawft-service-whisper runs on its own node, subscribes to PCM, publishes transcripts.
What's missing: there is no consumer in weft (or in the chat agent's inbound dispatch) that:
1. Subscribes to the transcript topic on the substrate.
2. Pushes each transcript as an agent.chat inbound message into the running agent's conversation.
3. OR routes transcripts as commands (e.g. transcripts matching weft <verb> patterns invoke the CLI verb).
Without this, the substrate produces transcripts and nothing listens. Voice ships as "transcripts-to-nowhere".
The 5 P0 voice security controls (SC-1/4/7/9/10 — WEFT-207/208/209/210/211) all attach at this consumer boundary, so they cannot be implemented or tested end-to-end until this wiring lands.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] A new substrate consumer (likely in clawft-weave/src/voice_router.rs or under clawft-service-agent) subscribes to the transcript topic at boot.
[ ] When a transcript arrives, it is dispatched to the running agent via the existing agent.chat RPC path (i.e. the same path the VSCode panel uses), with source: "voice" metadata so the agent + audit log know the origin.
[ ] A separate routing pass: transcripts that begin with the weft  prefix (configurable) are parsed as CLI verbs and invoked through the same RPC dispatch the panel uses (subject to permission gating per SC-4 / WEFT-208).
[ ] Configuration: ~/.clawft/config.json gains a voice.consumer section with enabled: bool, transcript_topic: string, chat_target_agent: string, command_prefix: string.

file: .planning/explorer/PROJECT-PLAN.md:14-26 (2026-04-23 incident postmortem)
Problem / gap
The VSCode extension's ALLOWED_METHODS allowlist is hand-maintained and drifts from the daemon dispatch table on a multi-day lag. The 2026-04-23 incident (chip icons grey because substrate.read was absent from the allowlist) was caused by exactly this gap. Every new daemon verb the WASM panel needs requires (a) a code edit in extension.ts and (b) re-running npm run compile. There is no automated extraction from daemon.rs:dispatch() and no shared canonical list.
Options:
(a) emit a JSON manifest from the daemon at boot and have the extension fetch it,
(b) generate a static allowed_methods.ts from a shared schema crate,
(c) move enforcement into the daemon (per-method capability tags + caller identity).
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Decision recorded (likely as ADR addendum) on which option to pursue.
[ ] Single source of truth lands; extension ALLOWED_METHODS either auto-syncs or becomes redundant.
[ ] CI gate fails when daemon verbs and extension allowlist drift.
[ ] Audit row marked closed with WEFT-N reference.
Dependencies
relates-to: ws15 daemon-side capability gating (option c)
Notes
Audit task list item #1.

WEFT-481.name: ws15: ipc_tcp relay — security audit (auth + bind-address default)
WEFT-481.description:
Source
audit: .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/15-mcp-integration.md (Status & Timeline, task list item #15)
config: [kernel.ipc_tcp] block wraps UDS in a byte-copy TCP relay
Problem / gap
The optional [kernel.ipc_tcp] relay exposes the same JSON wire format as the UDS socket over TCP. Combined with the lack of daemon-side per-method gating (separate item), this turns into a network-exposed RPC surface with no auth. Need explicit auth model + bind-address default of 127.0.0.1 only, plus documentation in the security review.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Default bind address is 127.0.0.1 (loopback only) unless explicitly overridden.
[ ] Document auth model (token? mTLS? local-uid check?) and ship a default that fails closed.
[ ] Add startup warning if relay binds to non-loopback without auth configured.
[ ] Security review doc updated to cover the relay attack surface.

Audit task list item #15.

WEFT-480.name: ws15: mcp-server — PermissionFilter::new(None) exposes every tool
WEFT-480.description:
Source
audit: .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/15-mcp-integration.md (Deferred items)
file: crates/clawft-cli/src/commands/mcp_server.rs:140 — PermissionFilter::new(None) at server boot
Problem / gap
weft mcp-server boots its middleware pipeline with PermissionFilter::new(None) — meaning no allowlist is applied; every registered tool (built-in, skill-derived, MCP-proxied) is exposed to the connecting MCP client. The security boundary today is SecurityGuard (command + URL policy) + ResultGuard (output truncation) + audit logging, but per-tool gating per session is not enforced. External MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor) connecting via stdio thus get the full surface.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Replace PermissionFilter::new(None) with a real per-tool allowlist sourced from config (e.g. tools.mcp_server.allowed_tools).
[ ] Document the default policy (deny-by-default vs allow-by-default) in MCP server docs.
[ ] Add a unit test confirming a tool not on the allowlist is rejected with a clear error.
[ ] Audit row marked closed with WEFT-N reference.
Dependencies
relates-to: ws15 daemon-side capability gating
Notes
Audit task list item #7.

WEFT-479.name: ws15: daemon RPC — no per-method capability gating on UDS callers
WEFT-479.description:
Source
audit: .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/15-mcp-integration.md (Deferred items, Open questions)
file: crates/clawft-weave/src/daemon.rs (~75-arm dispatch, no allowlist gate)
file: extensions/vscode-weft-panel/src/extension.ts:24-93 (comment claims daemon's 'own capability check is the real gate' — aspirational)
Problem / gap
The daemon JSON-RPC over UDS accepts ALL methods from any caller that can connect to the socket. The VSCode extension's ALLOWED_METHODS is a webview containment fence only — it stops a malicious webview script from reaching arbitrary RPC, but the daemon itself does no gating. With the optional [kernel.ipc_tcp] relay this becomes a network-exposed surface. The extension comment block carefully documents that the daemon's 'own capability check is the real gate' — but grep -n allow.*method on daemon.rs returns nothing useful. Either the comment is aspirational or gating happens at a layer the audit did not reach.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Decide approach: per-method capability tags + caller identity, or daemon-side allowlist sourced from config.
[ ] Implement gating at daemon dispatch entry; reject unknown/unauthorized methods with explicit error.
[ ] Document which methods are exposed to which caller classes (webview, CLI, mcp-server, TCP relay).
[ ] Tests cover at least one denied-method case per caller class.
[ ] Audit row marked closed with WEFT-N reference.
Dependencies
relates-to: ws15 ipc_tcp security audit
relates-to: ws15 ALLOWED_METHODS shared canonical list
Notes
Audit task list item #2.
Once daemon-side gating lands, ALLOWED_METHODS becomes redundant or advisory.

WEFT-8.name: ws14: workspace deps — migrate clawft-* path-deps to [workspace.dependencies] inheritance
WEFT-8.description:
Source
audit: .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/14-deployment-release.md (finding #5: internal-dep version drift)
handoff: docs/handoff.md "Next-session plan" item #4
code: workspace Cargo.toml (workspace.package.version = 0.6.19) vs every internal clawft-* path-dep pinned at 0.6.6
Problem / gap
Cargo.toml workspace.package.version is at 0.6.19, but every internal
clawft-* path-dep is pinned at 0.6.6. Next cargo publish will break
because the published-version metadata won't agree with the workspace
version. The fix is mechanical: migrate internal deps to
[workspace.dependencies] inheritance so a single workspace.package.version
bump propagates atomically.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] All internal clawft-* path-deps in member crates use
      { workspace = true } inheritance, not pinned literals.
[ ] [workspace.dependencies] lists each internal crate once with
      path = "..." and version = "..." matching the workspace
      package version.
[ ] scripts/build.sh check clean.
[ ] cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq '.workspace_members'
      shows all members and cargo tree -p clawft-weave -e=normal shows
      single-version internal-dep edges (no duplicate versions).
[ ] scripts/build.sh native build clean (i.e. weft and weaver
      binaries link).
[ ] Audit row finding #5 in .planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/14-deployment-release.md
      is annotated as closed with this WEFT-N reference.
Dependencies
blocks: any 0.7.0 publish to crates.io
blocked-by: none
upstream / external: none
Notes
Estimated ~1 hour of mechanical edits per the handoff.
Touch every member crate's Cargo.toml under crates/ —
  git ls-files crates/*/Cargo.toml | xargs grep -l "clawft-" is the
  starting list.
Consider also bumping internal version = "0.6.19" on the same pass
  so the version field reflects reality (separate from but related to
  this fix).
